title: When to write one
aiStatement: The third time, write the skill down
analogy: Explain the sample, refine it, write the card.
agent: Ask the agent to turn this conversation into a skill
groundingLine: What works for people also works for AI
groundingNote: : a strong rule of thumb, not a law.

sunlight.title: Sunlight
sunlight.script: We are one level down, in the sunlit zone. Here we decide two things: when a task deserves a skill at all, and how to describe it so the model actually picks it.

borrowed-principles.title: Borrowed principles
borrowed-principles.script: From here on I borrow principles from engineering, information architecture and UX, and they all lean on one idea: what works for people also works for AI. I say that as a strong rule of thumb, not as a law.

why-a-rule-of-thumb.title: Why a rule of thumb
why-a-rule-of-thumb.script: It holds because the model acts only on what you hand it, like a capable newcomer on their first day. It is only a rule of thumb because there are places where it breaks, and I've put those in the notes on the next Slide for you to read.
